## Diagnosis

`parse_unquoted_value` (parser.py:123-125) reads the rest of the line with `_unquoted_value` (`[^\r\n]*`) and strips comments via `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part).rstrip()`. The comment regex requires whitespace *before* `#`.

For `KEY= # explanation`, `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`, line 24) already consumes the space after `=`, so the value part begins directly with `# explanation`. No whitespace precedes `#`, so nothing is stripped and the value becomes `"# explanation"` instead of `""`.

`KEY=#literal` and `KEY=a#b` correctly stay literal (no preceding whitespace), and quoting/exports/ordinary comments are unaffected.

## Change Plan

In `parse_binding` (parser.py:156-158), after `_equal_sign`, peek past optional whitespace: if the next char is `#`, the value is empty — consume the comment and set `value=""`. Otherwise parse the value as today. This distinguishes `KEY= #c` (whitespace then `#` → empty) from `KEY=#literal` (no whitespace → literal), preserving all other behavior. Add parser tests for both cases.
